We're your virtual care dream team of naturopathic doctors and nutritionists who

properties.name: Wisdom Medicine

We're your virtual care dream team of naturopathic doctors and nutritionists who believe what you're feeling matters as much as your lab work. From period cramps to hot flashes, we’ve got your back on the journey to better health—no judgment, just results!

- 100% satisfaction. After a year, if you don’t get the answers you’ve been looking for, we’ll work with you for free until you do. 

Finally, with Wisdom Medicine, you’ve found the women's health experts you've always been looking for.

## About

The US is experiencing the fastest expansion of Medicaid and commercial insurance coverage for doula services in perinatal health history — yet the infrastructure to support

properties.name: Loula (YC W23)
properties.description:
The US is experiencing the fastest expansion of Medicaid and commercial insurance coverage for doula services in perinatal health history — yet the infrastructure to support this workforce doesn't exist at scale. Loula is building it. 

We operate a provider network and software platform that enables independent doulas to credential with multiple health plans through a single, simple application, submit insurance claims in under five minutes, and receive guaranteed bi-monthly payment. We're currently operating across all California counties with 350+ doulas and 12 health plan contracts, and backed by Y Combinator, BBG Ventures, Meridian Street Capital, and Wellington Access Ventures.

## About

Matilda exists to improve the li

properties.name: Matilda. Digital Endometriosis and Gynaecology Care
properties.description:
Matilda exists to improve the lives of the 190 million people with endometriosis around the world. 

People with endometriosis face long, convoluted, and invalidating journeys, but not with Matilda, a one-stop digital platform providing evidence-based and affordable education, symptom tracking, behaviour change support, group therapy, and access to specialised clinicians all from your pocket!

‘Matilda: Endometriosis care in your pocket’ was born after clinician researchers Jo Morris (Pelvic Health Physiotherapist) and Dr Kevin Wernli (Physiotherapist with a PhD in persistent pain) took out first prize at the 2022 Perth Biodesign for Digital Health course with teammates Dr Niamh Troy (Biologist and Researcher) and Maggie Woloszyn (MBA, Femtech Founder). Passion to provide better care for people with painful conditions like endometriosis, and conviction that there was a better way has led to the development of a Matilda MVP, the formation of a lived experience and clinical advisory board, and Matilda’s first customers! Matilda was also a finalist in the 2022 Curtinnovation Awards, and won first prize at the Golden Ticket Pitchfest at the Freo Start Up Fest as part of West Tech Fest in December 2022.

Ovy Health is a Southeast Asia-based femtech company reimagining the future of women’s healthcare—starting with fertility.

Headquartered in Singapore, we are building an integrated ecosystem that combines technology, clinical care, and personalized wellness to help women take control of their reproductive health with confidence and clarity.

Our journey began with a simple yet overlooked truth: most women don’t get proactive support until something goes wrong. Fertility care is often reactive, costly, and emotionally isolating. At Ovy Health, we believe in flipping the script—giving women the tools to plan ahead, access smarter care earlier, and receive continuous support across every stage of life.

Whether it’s navigating PCOS, preparing for IVF, or simply tracking their cycles, our virtual nurse offers culturally relevant, medically guided support—on app and on WhatsApp.

But we’re not stopping there. Ovy Health is expanding into fertility clinics, diagnostics, and supplements—creating a full-stack solution for women’s health. We partner with hospitals, health ministries, and wellness brands to bridge the gap between medical care and everyday health choices.

We are trusted by top clinics across Indonesia, and expanding regionally into Malaysia and Singapore. Our community spans women trying to conceive, young professionals planning ahead, and health-conscious individuals seeking hormone-friendly care.

📌 Backed by medical advisors, supported by AI
📌 Designed for women in Asia, built for global relevance
📌 Where clinical science meets compassionate care

Your plan. Your power.
Ovy Health isn’t just building a product—we’re building the future of how women are cared for.

Miryam is reimagining maternal health through predictive technology, culturally centered care, and a bold mission to save lives.

Rooted in the lived experiences of Black mothers and backed by cutting-edge research, Miryam is an AI-powered maternal health platform designed to detect, predict, and help prevent complications before they become crises. We are building a future where Black mothers are seen, heard, and protected. 

Every day, Black women in the U.S. are 3 to 4 times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women. Miryam, a patent-pending device and care delivery system, was created to change that.

As a predictive digital health solution, Miryam leverages clinical and lived experience data to generate risk profiles, support care decision-making, and create culturally resonant interventions that address disparities in maternal morbidity and mortality. We work with healthcare providers, community-based organizations, and payers to build tools that put equity at the center of care.

Our mission:
To radically improve Black maternal health outcomes through innovation, intelligence, and compassion.

Our vision:
A world where no mother is lost due to bias, delay, or preventable harm.

Whether you're a clinician, hospital system, public health agency, birth worker, researcher, or policymaker, we welcome collaboration.

Built by a Black mothers, for Black mothers.
Powered by science.
Designed for impact.
—
Follow Miryam for updates on product development, partnerships, research insights, and funding opportunities.
Visit us at: www.meetmiryam.com

Whether you’d like to grow your family soon or someday in the future, our mission is to help you create a personal plan based on unbiased information and quality research.

We call this your Fyrtle LifePlan. It is a uniquely crafted blueprint based on blending your significant achievements and unique life objectives with:

- Your desire and plans for parenthood, whether soon or in the future.
- Your reproductive health and overall wellness.
- Your relationship status and hopes for the future.
- Vital preconception tests for you to consider.

The Fyrtle LifePlan was largely conceived from Dr. Katie Haigh’s groundbreaking PhD research, which demonstrated significant knowledge gaps in individuals desiring future fertility and difficult access to this valuable information from health providers.

The Fyrtle team has worked in the fertility specialty area for many years. And what we’ve most commonly been told by our patients is, “I wish I had known about _____ a long time ago.” Our “Why” is to minimize those regrets for all people, and to start a dialog so you can ask us “Why” about topics that are important to you.

Our Vision: We envision a world where reproductive health and fertility information is accessible, actionable, and compassionate for all. Let Fyrtle guide you toward your future fertility with personalized care, expert support, and a LifePlan designed just for you.

Maven One Health improves the quality of provider data for health plans.

Imagine life-altering healthcare being delayed for you or someone you know because you couldn’t find the right doctor at the right time or because the information your insurer gave you was wrong. Imagine, in the midst of receiving critical care, that you get a huge, unexpected bill in the mail because you acted on incorrect information.

Our customizable Streamline workflow engine gives health plans the tools they need to manage workflows and operations, including additional data cleanup and operational business processes like contracting, credentialing, SIU/FWA investigations, and provider relations.

The platform is designed to help health plan carriers and partners of any level or size. It is also designed to help you save time and money with rapid, iterative implementations that deliver ROI early and often.

Visit our website today to get the expert help you need with your provider data.

properties.name: MAVEN
properties.description:
MAVEN is youth-focused. We are passionate about young people. Youth. Students. Junior highers. High schoolers. College students. The next generation. Because of our love for youth, we are also passionate about the people who disciple the next generation. Parents. Grandparents. Pastors. Youth leaders. Organizational leaders. Educators. We want to come alongside them to partner, guide, encourage, teach, train and equip them to raise up the next generation for the cause of Christ.

Gender identity. Sexual orientation. Pornography. Casual sex. Consumerism. Affluence. Substance abuse. Violence. Technology. Social media. Entertainment. Racial tension. Pluralism. Secularism. Atheism.

Are they ready for these conversations? Are we? The typical evangelical kid in our typical evangelical church is not. Neither are their parents or leaders. Rather than bemoan the situation and give in to despair, the church needs to redouble her efforts in discipling the next generation. And we need to do it in culturally-savvy and relevant ways, while never compromising the truth of Christ.

We must repackage and re-present the truth to media-saturated students who have been raised on screens and images. We must wrap the truth in culturally savvy ways that grab the attention of their distracted minds, gain a hearing and woo them back to Christ. We need a new brand—a new movement—to reach that kind of kid. That’s why we need MAVEN.

It lets you scan any cosmetic or food product and instantly see what to avoid, what to limit, and what's actually beneficial for your specific stage and health conditions.

It monitors, adjusts, and nudges proactively, like having a nutritionist and personal trainer who know your full situation and are always on call.

Because PregSafe draws from our own verified sources and expert-backed databases rather than the open internet, the risk of hallucination is massively reduced compared to general-purpose Al tools. We have a growing waitlist, strong early conversion, and we're heading into alpha testing with a nutritionist and toxicologist on our advisory team.

At the heart of the platform is a proprietary cosmetic ingredient database of 590+ flagged ingredients, cross-referenced against ECHA, PubMed, FDA, EU SCCS, and EWG, verified by a toxicologist. Combined with a food product database of over 4 million products and a curated knowledge base of peer-reviewed research and clinical guidelines, PregSafe delivers guidance women can actually trust.

Indonesia’s GP‑first virtual front door — clinically governed care, cashless referrals, and 20–40% lower health cost leakage.

CallMyDokter is Indonesia’s clinically governed virtual care platform that improves health outcomes, reduces 20–40% cost leakage, and strengthens long‑term patient–doctor relationships. We deliver unlimited GP‑led telemedicine, chronic‑care support, women’s‑health programs, wellness pathways, and seamless referrals through a GP‑first triage model that ensures patients receive the right care at the right time.

Indonesia faces major health and cost challenges: 70% of outpatient costs come from chronic conditions, 50% of sick leave is linked to unmanaged disease, and 1 in 3 women miss work monthly due to menstrual pain. Patients see the same doctor who understands their history, monitors progress, and guides their health journey. This improves outcomes, reduces avoidable claims, and supports healthier, more productive workforces.

We akso work with insurers and TPAs to ensure members are referred to the right physical care when needed, supported by cashless access and integrated claims processes that simplify care for companies and employees. Our platform connects virtual and physical care into one coordinated experience.

Our tools include quality video, online booking system, concierge support, integrated medical records, medication governance, chronic‑care and women’s‑health pathways, seamless referrals, and cashless integration with insurer/TPA networks. Significant value is also achieved through our data‑driven insights that help employers and insurers reduce leakage and improve member outcomes.

CallMyDokter: Better care. Better outcomes. Lower cost.

Empowering women to lead with their whole selves is the work.

Whether a woman lives with us, builds her business in our spaces, or joins us for one of our experiences, our intention is the same: to empower her to do the inner work that allows her to show up grounded, clear, and connected, so she can lift others up too.

Because when women are empowered to become whole, they don’t just change their own lives. They change communities. And that’s how we create a brighter future for everyone.

entity.description:
Ovy Health is a Southeast Asia-based femtech company reimagining the future of women’s healthcare—starting with fertility.

Headquartered in Singapore, we are building an integrated ecosystem that combines technology, clinical care, and personalized wellness to help women take control of their reproductive health with confidence and clarity.

At Ovy Health, we believe in flipping the script—giving women the tools to plan ahead, access smarter care earlier, and receive continuous support across every stage of life.

Our flagship platform offers AI-powered pre-diagnosis, virtual patient concierge, and clinic-integrated care pathways, helping users make informed decisions about their fertility and hormonal health. Whether it’s navigating PCOS, preparing for IVF, or simply tracking their cycles, our virtual nurse offers culturally relevant, medically guided support—on app and on WhatsApp.

But we’re not stopping there. Ovy Health is expanding into fertility clinics, diagnostics, and supplements—creating a full-stack solution for women’s health. We partner with hospitals, health ministries, and wellness brands to bridge the gap between medical care and everyday health choices.

We are trusted by top clinics across Indonesia, and expanding regionally into Malaysia and Singapore. Our community spans women trying to conceive, young professionals planning ahead, and health-conscious individuals seeking hormone-friendly care.

📌 Backed by medical advisors, supported by AI
📌 Designed for women in Asia, built for global relevance
📌 Where clinical science meets compassionate care

Your plan. Your power.
Ovy Health isn’t just building a product—we’re building the future of how women are cared for.

entity.description:
Miryam is reimagining maternal health through predictive technology, culturally centered care, and a bold mission to save lives.

Rooted in the lived experiences of Black mothers and backed by cutting-edge research, Miryam is an AI-powered maternal health platform designed to detect, predict, and help prevent complications before they become crises. We are building a future where Black mothers are seen, heard, and protected. 

Every day, Black women in the U.S. are 3 to 4 times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women. Miryam, a patent-pending device and care delivery system, was created to change that.

As a predictive digital health solution, Miryam leverages clinical and lived experience data to generate risk profiles, support care decision-making, and create culturally resonant interventions that address disparities in maternal morbidity and mortality. We work with healthcare providers, community-based organizations, and payers to build tools that put equity at the center of care.

Our mission:
To radically improve Black maternal health outcomes through innovation, intelligence, and compassion.

Our vision:
A world where no mother is lost due to bias, delay, or preventable harm.

Whether you're a clinician, hospital system, public health agency, birth worker, researcher, or policymaker, we welcome collaboration.

Built by a Black mothers, for Black mothers.
Powered by science.
Designed for impact.
—
Follow Miryam for updates on product development, partnerships, research insights, and funding opportunities.

Whether you’d like to grow your family soon or someday in the future, our mission is to help you create a personal plan based on unbiased information and quality research.

We call this your Fyrtle LifePlan. It is a uniquely crafted blueprint based on blending your significant achievements and unique life objectives with:

- Your desire and plans for parenthood, whether soon or in the future.
- Your reproductive health and overall wellness.
- Your relationship status and hopes for the future.
- Vital preconception tests for you to consider.

The Fyrtle LifePlan was largely conceived from Dr. Katie Haigh’s groundbreaking PhD research, which demonstrated significant knowledge gaps in individuals desiring future fertility and difficult access to this valuable information from health providers.

The Fyrtle team has worked in the fertility specialty area for many years. And what we’ve most commonly been told by our patients is, “I wish I had known about _____ a long time ago.” Our “Why” is to minimize those regrets for all people, and to start a dialog so you can ask us “Why” about topics that are important to you.

Our Vision: We envision a world where reproductive health and fertility information is accessible, actionable, and compassionate for all. Let Fyrtle guide you toward your future fertility with personalized care, expert support, and a LifePlan designed just for you.

entity.name: PregSafe
entity.description:
PregSafe is an agentic AI assistant built specifically for women who are trying to conceive, pregnant, or breastfeeding.

It lets you scan any cosmetic or food product and instantly see what to avoid, what to limit, and what's actually beneficial for your specific stage and health conditions. 

But scanning is just the entry point. It builds meal plans that adjust day by day based on what you actually eat, your cycle phase or trimester, your energy levels, and real-time data from wearables like Oura and Apple Watch. It tailors exercise to your stage, your sleep quality, and your recovery. And it doesn't wait to be asked. It monitors, adjusts, and nudges proactively, like having a nutritionist and personal trainer who know your full situation and are always on call.

Because PregSafe draws from our own verified sources and expert-backed databases rather than the open internet, the risk of hallucination is massively reduced compared to general-purpose Al tools. We have a growing waitlist, strong early conversion, and we're heading into alpha testing with a nutritionist and toxicologist on our advisory team.

At the heart of the platform is a proprietary cosmetic ingredient database of 590+ flagged ingredients, cross-referenced against ECHA, PubMed, FDA, EU SCCS, and EWG, verified by a toxicologist. Combined with a food product database of over 4 million products and a curated knowledge base of peer-reviewed research and clinical guidelines, PregSafe delivers guidance women can actually trust.

Because safety isn't a yes/no question. It's personal.

PregSafe is pre-launch and building its waitlist now

entity.name: Call My Dokter
entity.description:
Indonesia’s GP‑first virtual front door — clinically governed care, cashless referrals, and 20–40% lower health cost leakage.

CallMyDokter is Indonesia’s clinically governed virtual care platform that improves health outcomes, reduces 20–40% cost leakage, and strengthens long‑term patient–doctor relationships. We deliver unlimited GP‑led telemedicine, chronic‑care support, women’s‑health programs, wellness pathways, and seamless referrals through a GP‑first triage model that ensures patients receive the right care at the right time.

Indonesia faces major health and cost challenges: 70% of outpatient costs come from chronic conditions, 50% of sick leave is linked to unmanaged disease, and 1 in 3 women miss work monthly due to menstrual pain. Unmet women’s‑health needs create silent productivity loss, while chat‑based telemedicine produces poor outcomes, low diagnostic accuracy, fragmented care, and unnecessary escalation.

CallMyDokter replaces “any doctor, anytime” chat models with continuous, relationship‑based care. You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.

    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.

      entries fail.

  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of

                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does

  this company to be in the same market?

    - A different category fails, even for the same customer

      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.
